speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I understand you are experiencing right groin pain and noticed your leg was positioned abnormally after a rear-end collision. To begin my assessment, can you describe the exact moment the injury occurred and whether you heard a specific sound like a snap or pop at the time?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Cruciate Ligament (PCL) Injury with concurrent hip pathology. The mechanism of injury (rear-end collision with the unrestrained or restrained driver's knees striking the dashboard) is classic for a PCL tear, and the immediate severe groin pain suggests potential involvement of the hip joint or femoral head. Please confirm if you felt a "pop" and if you have any difficulty bearing weight on the right leg. REQUEST TEST: MRI Right Knee and Hip. REQUEST IMAGES: T2-weighted MRI sequences of the right knee and hip.
